schema_version: v1 — 2026-09-01, hex ids, merged falsifier, engineer-readable
what: Cast nodes — an intention that has passed /sorted, been typed to a node-class and bound to that class's gate-set. The universal work unit.
why: Workflow rides on node-class, not on the node's identity, so a ticket carries no domain — an 'inference ticket' and a 'concept-piece ticket' are the same artifact with a different class field. Everybody has tickets. Crucially, the ticket's `workflow_and_state` field IS the pipeline instance: no orchestrator holds a second copy of where the work stands, so the state of the tickets is the state of all things, always (MAP.md 'Gates, not supervisors'). Written when skill:/sorted casts a node.
owner: each ticket has exactly one owner who gates writes to it; the owner alone advances its state through the bound gates (Law 6). The tickets store owns the collection; the emit chokepoint validates records against the template.
filename: <hex-id>-<title-slug>.json — hex is the stable machine identifier, slug is the human handle

template.id: string — 12-char hex, the stable machine identifier (uuid4 minted at cast time)
template.title: string — the human-readable one-liner (kebab-case slug)
template.owner: who gates writes (terse — a name, not a paragraph)
template.owning_intention: path to the intention+why.json that owns this ticket
template.intention: what this node is FOR (the WHAT)

falsifier.proves_green: what the proof gate checks — the conditions that mean it worked
falsifier.proves_red: what would show this node wrong — the conditions that mean it went wrong
falsifier.horizon: when to re-check (optional — omit if testable now)

template.children: array — child ticket hex ids, or 'none, because <X>'
template.questions: array of {q, a} — the challenge answers and open questions
template.constraints: array — what the build must respect
template.links: array — parent tickets, decisions, cited_by references
template.node_class: the bound class (address in node_classes/): skill | concept-piece | code-seam | …
template.workflow_and_state: the pipeline instance — the full workflow cursor string
template.watchme: object — the probe spec the emission gate reads, or null
template.deposits: object — {stage_name: stage_output} where the chart pipeline writes its cargo
template.sorted_berth: path — the sorted door's berth for this cast
template.chart_claim: path — the chart chain's claim, or null

entry.the_three_doors: IDEA (pre-intention design) → INTENT (/intent births and traces) → TICKET. This store is a DIRECT entry point, not only /sorted's output: a bug enters here without passing IDEA or INTENT.
entry.what_makes_it_structural_instead: LEVEL, not size or effort. Akien verbatim: 'if we have to edit lines of code to fix it, then it's not deeply structural... but if new information breaks the harmony of the system (eg an intention was implemented in a way contrary to the actual intention) with that version you and i have to reconcile it. that's structural.' A structural bug is reconciled with Akien; it does not enter here unexamined.
entry.why_the_test_is_shaped_this_way: The cost heuristic CC reaches for by default — big, scary, wide blast radius — is a judgment call, so it drifts. Akien's test names an OBSERVABLE: look at where the fix lands. Same move as intention+why.json forcing the why into the filename (Law 4 in miniature).

notes_on_the_store: TROUBLES DRAIN HERE. troubles/ is a pre-ticket inbox, not a parallel place work lives; a trouble that never becomes a ticket is a bug with no workflow. The trouble record stays (it is the account of the live symptom); the ticket is what moves through the gates.
A ticket is never terminal: `validated` = best guess still carrying its falsifier and horizon; the back-edge (build → deconstruct) is the universal shape.
A node with no falsifier does not cast (the /sorted completeness gate).
Ownership stays put; what moves phase-to-phase is which peer is invited to act next, through the owner's gate — not a transfer of ownership.
